meta.title: what actually deserves a model?
meta.subtitle: we kept trying to make routing smarter. the useful part was figuring out which decisions should not be model problems at all.
meta.author: zer0 research
meta.lede: we spent a week trying to make automatic routing smarter. the funniest result was how often the dumb deterministic thing won.

banner.tag: mixed evidence · some stuff worked, some stuff got wrecked
banner.text: jev held up. nanojev got exposed. julia reproduced and still lost on the real routing task. the provider path physically ran. delegation did not save parent work. the memory result lives in its own post.

nanojev.verdict: The training objective cannot support this primitive. The success criterion was not met, and the target ordering is inverted. Integration stopped.

local_config.loss: per-question forward soft CE, equal question weight; complete candidate normalization

boolean_defect.why: the first logit is multiplied by zero, so `false` is a constant rather than a measured probability; the boolean path is also excluded from the trained attention set head
boolean_defect.consequence: correcting the contrast removed most of the apparent signal

nanojev.trainer_location: not in any branch of the repository; established from the publisher's recipe and config, not a local trainer
nanojev.lesson: Fast ≠ suitable objective. Interface compatibility is not capability equivalence.

jev.proxy_correction: Our first reproduction attempt tested proxy models instead of the model the paper used. A reproduction of a different system is not a reproduction.

binary_slice.caveat: AUROC 0.9982 applies ONLY to this binary slice. Computed over all 144 rows with a different slice definition it is 0.5686 — the number is slice-dependent and must be quoted with its slice.

class_gap.disclosure: A perfect 1.0000 on a set with no `insufficient` gold label does not exercise the hardest class in authored144 and cannot support a general abstention claim.

omitted.why: our recomputation used a different formulation (per-class, 0.6025) and we will not publish a number we could not reproduce

abandoned_target.text: The originally targeted 146:4 AbstentionBench slice is not present in this checkout and was a poor primary reproduction target: at a 97% majority class a single accuracy number is dominated by the majority, and it does not exercise the three-way contract the runtime routes on.

claims.text: A green benchmark historically did not prove workers physically executed; execution is only established by a canonical receipt with provider-assigned identity, tokens and latency.
Jev 1.13.0 reaches 0.9514 family-balanced accuracy and 0.0334 ECE on authored144, and 0.9982 AUROC with 0.9524 balanced accuracy on the 48-example binary abstention slice.
AUROC 0.9982 holds only for the binary abstention slice; over all 144 rows with a different slice definition it is 0.5686.
perturbations108 scores 1.0000 but contains no `insufficient` gold label.
claims.evidence: gold id census of the raw file

claims.text: NanoJev was trained for game/action-choice tasks and its boolean path used a degenerate contrast; correcting it removed most of the apparent signal.
claims.evidence: publisher recipe + local config + source inspection

claims.text: On both measured cohorts delegation increased parent work; Cerebras kept automatic generic-worker delegation ineligible despite 60/60 worker quality.
No token or dollar saving from delegation is claimed.
claims.evidence: measured direction is negative at the tested sizes

claims.text: Per-provider headroom (Cerebras/DeepSeek/Jev large headroom, a Groq wall, a lower NVIDIA wall) is not reproduced here.
claims.evidence: source report states its ~330-probe reference was not recovered

claims.text: Provider concurrency caps are policy inputs, not measurements. Only the 32-admission test is measured.
claims.evidence: 64-request burst against the authority, counted local fixture

claims.text: Completed duplicates replay, a same-trace different-request is rejected without a second physical execution, and an uncertain prior execution is refused.
A real free-only execution on a provider-reported $0 route returned the expected output with one canonical physical start/completion.
Laya remains capability-local and experimental; on the sealed real-trace tool-family task it scored 19.48%, below a 51.95% majority and a 74.03% deterministic keyword rule.
Julia-1 is faithfully integrated and very fast, but failed the real-trace routing task (10.39% sealed accuracy); its confidence ranking is unusable as a safe cascade gate, so it remains default-off.
Production readiness remains bounded, but the routing/authority layer is now canonical; the executor is still a single-replica lane with no autoscaler and billing remains unverified.
claims.evidence: canonical z0intelligence routing PR + deployment/lifecycle receipts

claims.text: The published Brier 0.0408 is not reproduced by our formulation and is therefore not claimed.
The first pinned multimodal decision lane is reproducible and produced 4/8 on the eight published examples; no public-split, sealed, latency or official Image JevBench score is claimed.
OMP provider usage is accumulated across turns and only marked complete when all observed turns carry provider usage; Tokenomics preserves the measurement state instead of upgrading proxies.

sources.role: canonical verifier metadata, decision backends, dispatch authority, worker routing, receipts

limitations: The router, service, dispatch authority and provider-saturation modules live in an unpublished local revision and are not yet in canonical main.
Provider concurrency caps are policy inputs; the referenced ~330-probe report was not reproduced.
Per-provider headroom is UNKNOWN in this evidence set.
Both delegation cohorts are repeated runs of a small fixed task set (2 pairs; 30 repeats of each of two tasks), not task-population samples.
Parent cache exposure was measured and stratified, not randomized; only one Cerebras pair had zero cache in both arms.
The Cerebras high-reasoning cohort completed 4/60 pairs and is excluded rather than pooled.
The 146:4 AbstentionBench slice originally targeted is not present in the checkout.
Estimated parent tokens avoided is a bytes/4 baseline, not a measured counterfactual.
No dollar savings are claimed; billing is unverified in both delegation cohorts.
The Kubernetes lane is a single replica with no autoscaler; scaling a proxy would not increase model capacity.
Reboot availability of the host service was not tested.
Wrong test runner and a silently-skipping schema cross-check were both found during this work; the corrected baseline is quoted in Methods.

methods.s: 5 live-marked failures (network/provider), 3 skipped, with declared runtime deps installed incl. torch 2.10.0
running the wrong runner against a unittest-declared suite produced 142 false errors on a healthy repo
necessary but not sufficient: a branch read as 'genuinely new' by patch-id had already landed under a rewritten SHA with an extra fix on top
a skill merged without textual conflict and still violated a newer frontmatter contract
reports success while verifying nothing when an optional dependency is absent
Jev metrics were recomputed from the per-example JSONL rather than copied from shipped constants
